minutes.headline: Sewer Commission leaned toward deferring a bylaw waiver wording change to next May; a deferral motion was made, vote not captured.
minutes.summary: Lou Franco asked the commission to back a further amendment to the sewer bylaw's waiver criterion, changing "best interest of the town" to "not counter to the interests of the town". Most members liked the wording but wanted to wait until next May's town meeting, citing a pending development project and the long town meeting debate. A deferral motion was made and seconded; the captions end before a vote.

votes.motion: Defer the proposed waiver wording amendment until next May's meeting; seconded.

decisions.decision: Lou Franco said he could accept deferral, and he agreed to return to help next May; the commissioners' inclination was to wait.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission leaned toward waiting until next May's town meeting to change the sewer bylaw's waiver wording, and a deferral motion was made and seconded.
The captions end before a vote on the deferral, so the outcome is not recorded in these minutes.
Lou Franco proposed changing the waiver criterion from "best interest of the town" to "not counter to the interests of the town".
Franco said he could accept deferral and would return to help next May.

why_it_matters: The waiver criterion in the sewer bylaw decides how easily an exception can be granted, and any change to it would go before voters at town meeting, so a deferral keeps the current wording in force until at least next May.
watch_next: Whether the deferral vote is recorded in the commission's official minutes for 13 September 2022.
Whether the waiver amendment appears on the warrant for next May's town meeting.
